response:
It makes sense that you're feeling torn. You've spent a long time managing a difficult relationship, and wanting to protect your own peace during the holidays is completely valid—not selfish.

It might help to weigh what you actually want against what you fear will happen if you don't go. Sometimes the anxiety of anticipated conflict is heavier than the reality. You could consider a middle path if that feels right: a shorter visit, a phone call, or spending part of the holiday with people who do feel supportive. If you decide not to attend, a brief, calm message setting that boundary is enough—you don't owe a lengthy justification.

Whatever you choose, try to prioritize what helps you feel safe and steady. If this is bringing up a lot of distress, talking it through with a therapist or a trusted friend could give you some clarity and support. You deserve to spend the holidays in a way that respects your wellbeing.
